name: news-20260710-llm-wiki-knowledge-context
title: LLM Wiki and Knowledge Context — Team Knowledge Compiled at Write Time
summary: Analyzes a seminar talk, with original-source checks and diagrams, covering Karpathy's LLM Wiki (write-time compilation vs RAG), the promotion flow of an Obsidian+Git team implementation, OpenViking's layered loading, and human/agent governance.

relations.evidenceRef: Karpathy's LLM Wiki gist, OpenViking and other primary sources checked — backs the course concepts of llmw-overview

name: news-20260710-oracle-ontology-property-graph
title: Oracle Ontology and Property Graphs — Turning Tables into a Map of Knowledge
summary: Organizes Oracle's ontology and property graph approach — RDF vs property graphs, building a graph as a metadata view, PGQL and SQL/PGQ multi-hop and cycle queries, graph algorithms, and Select AI natural-language querying, explained with official-doc verification, diagrams, and a glossary.

relations.evidenceRef: Oracle's official blog and ISO SQL:2023 checked — external evidence for sb-level4's claim that knowledge is linked by relationship

name: news-20260711-neo4j-rdf-vs-property-graph
title: RDF or Property Graph — Two Models for a Knowledge Graph (Neo4j)
summary: A write-up of Neo4j's Jim Webber on 'RDF vs property graphs' (2024) — a knowledge graph's entities, relationships, and organizing principle; the limits of RDF triples and the semantic web (relationships not first-class, SPARQL termination, ontology upkeep); the property graph's advantages with the NASA, Basecamp, and Novo Nordisk cases; ISO GQL; and the conclusion "property graph by default + an ontology layer when needed".

relations.evidenceRef: A digest of the Neo4j original by Jim Webber (2024-06-04) — expert evidence for sb-level4's knowledge-graph approach

name: news-20260716-kimi-k3
title: Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model reaches the frontier
summary: A web-search cross-checked roundup of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 launch (2.8T total with ~50B active MoE, KDA and AttnRes) — benchmarks such as 3rd on the AA index and 1st in Frontend Arena, $3/$15 pricing, long-horizon autonomous demos like chip design and gravitational-wave analysis, and the self-reported vs independently reproduced gap alongside cyber risk and market fallout.

relations.evidenceRef: Terminal-Bench 2.1 with its own harness (KimiCode) 88.3 vs Vals' independent reproduction ~80.9 — measured evidence for hns-what's argument that the harness and its configuration decide the outcome

name: news-20260728-software-factories-fail
title: The Harness Is Not Enough — Why Software Factories Fail
summary: Dex Horthy (HumanLayer) at AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 — models are rewarded only for passing tests, never for design quality, so no harness can close the gap; Faros telemetry (bugs +54%, incidents tripled), a failed four-month lights-out experiment, FrontierCode scoring maintainability, and 30 minutes of four-step alignment before any code

name: news-20260724-snucatch-ai-coding
title: The End of Coding by Hand? — The Future of Developers as Seen by SNU's Prof. Jaewook Lee
summary: A write-up of the SNU Catch Season 2 talk with Prof. Jaewook Lee (SNU Computer Science and Engineering, director of the AI Institute) plus web cross-checking — the argument that implementation is nearly 100% automated while problem definition and critique remain, the power of vibe coding and the 95% trap, the education problem of students becoming couriers and an AI-native curriculum, the lessons of the Jevons paradox and bank tellers after the ATM, and entry-level developer employment at -20% (Stanford/ADP) alongside METR's measured 19%.

name: news-20260724-claude-opus-5
title: Claude Opus 5 — A Near-Fable at Half the Price Has Arrived
summary: A cross-verified account of Anthropic's 2026-07-24 Claude Opus 5 launch from the official announcement and multiple press reports — at $5/$25 it lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's CursorBench 3.2 max peak at half the cost per task, with Frontier-Bench 43.3%, OSWorld 2.0 on ⅓ the budget and 3× on ARC-AGI 3, a long-horizon agentic demo that wrote its own CV pipeline to rebuild FreeCAD 3D when it could not view the drawing, plus the context of the Fable 5 safeguard false-positive controversy and a separation of unconfirmed claims

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-plan-a
title: AI 2040: Plan A — Overview (the normative scenario that says delay superintelligence until 2040)
summary: The overview and hub of a commentary series on the follow-up normative scenario from the authors of AI 2027 (AI Futures Project) — a recommendation rather than a prediction, covering the core idea of delaying superintelligence to 2040 through a US-China agreement, the one-line gist, an interactive timeline and a comparison with AI 2027, and pointing to the three installments on the scenario, the policy and the reactions

relations.evidenceRef: Overview and hub — it sets up the four-part structure and the background (a recommendation, not a forecast), so it precedes the year-by-year scenario detail

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-scenario
title: AI 2040: Plan A — the year-by-year scenario (2027 → 2040)
summary: The world Plan A paints year by year — 2027 two workforces (humans + AI agents), 2028 the election and data center costs, 2029 the US-China agreement, 2030 averting full automation, 2030-35 expansion to expert level, 2035 a pause to keep control, 2040 the release and superintelligence, stated explicitly as a recommendation rather than a prediction

relations.evidenceRef: Assumes the year-by-year world the scenario draws, then reads the policy and verification that hold it up (body: 'Next — policy and verification')

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-policy

summary: The mechanisms that hold the deal together — total research transparency, the verification protocol (network taps and partial recomputation), SL5 security, relocated data centers (US to Mongolia, China to Canada), mutually assured compute destruction, the model spec and third-party oversight; the original's interactive Supplements explorer is carried here only as a static summary

relations.evidenceRef: After understanding the policy and verification machinery, read the support and criticism it drew (body: 'Next — Reactions and critiques')

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-reactions
title: AI 2040: Plan A — Reactions and Critiques
summary: A board of support and criticism after the release. Richard Ngo's three objections (the ambiguity of an optimistic forecast, the 2040 handover of power, the politics of optimism, published alongside at the authors' request), Dave Friedman (technical legibility is not political feasibility), Rohit Krishnan (underspecified terms), plus coverage from Scott Alexander, WaPo and Axios

name: news-20260801-astra-math
title: OpenAI Astra — “Ten Open Problems Solved”, and This Time It Brought Certificates
summary: A cross-verified account of OpenAI's 2026-08-01 claim that an internal Astra solved ten decade-old open problems (first non-sofic group after 27 years, a disproof of Connes rigidity, the first sphere-packing bound improvement since 1978, and more) — the verification system of Lean machine-checked certificates plus named expert readers (Popa et al.), the pre-peer-review caveat, Tao's 'proof abundance' frame and Bloom's reaction, contrasted with the October 2025 GPT-5 Erdős fiasco

name: news-20260803-cherny-karpathy
title: The One Who Deleted and the One Who Rendered — Cherny's “80% of the Harness” and Karpathy's “LOTR Movie”
summary: Two scenes from right after Opus 5, cross-verified into one piece — Claude Code creator Cherny deleted 80%+ of the system prompt and the model got smarter (ablation methodology, 'sabotage yourselves every six months', 'loops prompt Claude'), while Karpathy turned LOTR's first paragraph plus $10 into a 5,500-line three.js 3D movie, embedded playable in the article. The shared structure: scaffolding shrinks × output scale jumps × the bottleneck moves to verification and perception

name: news-20260814-auto-mode-stateless-mcp
title: Defaults That Stop Asking — Auto Mode and Stateless MCP
summary: Two changes from the same week in one piece — from 2026-08-14 Claude Code makes auto mode the default for new Pro, Max, and Team sessions (97% of prompts approved, people refused a planted dangerous command only 13.6% of the time, the classifier blocked 89%, and Trajectory Labs saw zero successes across 720 injection attempts), while the MCP 2026-07-28 spec deleted the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id to take state out of the protocol (_meta, server/discover, server-minted handles, Tasks/MCP Apps/enterprise authorization extensions, wire-incompatible both ways). The shared structure: remove the fixed point held at runtime and move the decision to declared rules and per-request data

name: wr-knowledge-vault
title: The Man Who Records Everything, and the Wiki That Publishes — Reflections on Knowledge Vaults
summary: Starting from the questions 'is this wiki RAG, an LLM wiki, or a second brain?', this reflection dissects the conversation transcript of a lifelogging practitioner who streams his entire life — 24-hour audio and screen capture — into a note vault, and compares his system with this wiki: the five-layer daily note (intent, execution, reality, interpretation, AI logs), the raw/wiki vault split and an ingest that asks back 'why did you keep this?' (motive as data), RAG vs LLM wiki as query-time vs keep-time tidying, the maxim that an ontology is a document rather than a graph, and the failure theory that purposeless hoarding breeds tombs of knowledge. It closes with four steps for this wiki: explicit capture motives, automated monthly retrospectives, a private inbox layer, and a conversational QA entry point

name: gdb-graphrag
title: Graph Databases & GraphRAG — Store the Relationships, Change the Answers
summary: An introductory explainer that chains graph databases to GraphRAG in one pass — property graphs that walk edges instead of computing JOINs and Cypher, the query language that looks like the drawing; GraphRAG stitching vector RAG's severed chunks back into a web so retrieval brings the whole neighborhood (multi-hop reasoning, preserved hierarchy, drawable evidence); ontology and graph schema as the web's blueprint (prerequisite relations in an education knowledge map); the similarly named stranger LangGraph (map of knowledge vs flowchart of work); domain cases from manufacturing failure logs to news categories; and a getting-started path from arrows.app sketches through Cypher export to turning a PDF into a knowledge graph with the neo4j-graphrag package (SimpleKGPipeline)

name: gdb-vector-retriever
title: Finding a Movie by Its Story — Your First Vector Retriever on a Neo4j Sandbox
summary: The hands-on companion to the concepts piece — borrow a graph DB in the browser with Neo4j Sandbox (the MovieLens-family Recommendations dataset: Movie, Genre, Actor, Director and User nodes, plus a RATED relationship that carries data), stroll the data with a few lines of Cypher, embed 100 movie plots into 1,536-dimensional vectors with an OpenAI embedding model and plant them as a plotEmbedding property, add a CREATE VECTOR INDEX (cosine similarity), then assemble a searcher with neo4j-graphrag's VectorRetriever (four parameters: driver, index, embedder, return properties). Summarise Toy Story's plot and the movie comes back in first place without its title ever being mentioned — the feel of vector search finding stories rather than words, and the next step toward GraphRAG: cast with vectors, walk with the graph

name: sks-im-not-ai
title: im-not-ai (Humanize KR) — An Editing Skill That Erases the AI Tell
summary: AI-written text gives itself away through habits, not grammar — an introduction to im-not-ai, an editing skill that finds and removes 33 traces such as inflated significance, aphorism formulas, signposting, fake candor, mechanical rule-of-three, and vague attribution. The body is blader's humanizer (MIT) vendored verbatim; its root is Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing". Covers the equally important false-positive half (judge by clusters of tells, preserve human signals, the author's sample outranks the rules, facts are immutable, respect the genre), the draft → two-question audit → final loop, installation and invocation, and this wiki's field record of passing all 121 indexed documents × 3 languages through it — only about 22 sentences of edits, with the style audit catching factual errors (7→9 views, a table summing wrong) along the way

relations.evidenceRef: The article delegates what a skill physically is (one markdown file in a folder) to 'What is a Skill' and builds the install/trigger explanation on top of it

name: tip-beginner
title: Beginner — 9 Habits That Save Context
summary: Nine starter tips for Claude Code, each checked against the official docs — /init to generate CLAUDE.md, the status line, keeping context small, hunting token hogs with /context, /compact vs /clear, plan mode (and what it means now that auto mode is the default), asking with problems not functions, the 95% ask-me-back prompt, and planting self-checks into to-dos

name: tip-intermediate
title: Intermediate — 11 Ways to Turn Sessions into a System
summary: Eleven tips for moving repetition into the system — parallel subagents (own context, summary-only reporting), building your own skills, running subagents on Haiku, updating CLAUDE.md with a 150–200 line cap, CLAUDE.md as a router, interrupting mid-run (Esc), pushing back then recording what works, /rewind checkpoints, hook notifications, image input, and screenshot-to-template

name: tip-advanced
title: Advanced — 8 Tips for Parallel, Autonomous, Scheduled Work
summary: Eight tips for parallel, autonomous, scheduled work — collision-free parallel sessions with claude --worktree, calling APIs directly instead of MCP (context cost), the three tiers of scheduling (/loop, desktop tasks, cloud Routines), phone remote control via claude remote-control, natural-language database queries, ultrathink and OMC's consensus-based ralplan, editing permissions in settings.json (auto mode's hard denies), and subagents vs agent teams (plus OMC's team mode)

name: gdb-onto-concepts
title: What Is an Ontology — Not a Warehouse of Data but a Map of Meaning
summary: The concept questions enterprise practitioners ask most, organized around an anonymized Korean webinar FAQ — a database is a warehouse storing values while an ontology is a map defining meaning, relations, and rules (Gruber's 'explicit specification of a conceptualization', W3C OWL 2); the four essential components (core concepts, relations, data, rules); the semantic layer as an interpreter between legacy (ERP·CRM·MES) and generative AI (not a migration; Palantir's 'digital twin of an organization' as precedent); why better LLMs still need ontologies (hallucination — OG-RAG's +55% fact recall, a clinical QA study cutting hallucination 63%→1.7%, an ontology query language constraining the LLM's degrees of freedom); and the graph DB as just one of three stores (RDB·vector·graph) an ontology orchestrates

relations.evidenceRef: Delegates knowledge graph / GraphRAG / 'fish with vectors, walk with graphs' concepts to the GraphRAG article and builds the ontology layer on top

name: gdb-onto-adoption
title: How Companies Adopt Ontologies — Cases · ROI · The Four-Step Build
summary: The practice part following the concepts — industry cases (finance's regulation-change tracing and claim adjudication, manufacturing's causal failure analysis, risk assessment and QMS quality tracing, SCM's inventory cause analysis) and the position as the stage before digital twins; ROI evolving from operating-cost savings to automation to restructuring revenue-linked work (plus the opportunity-cost view of decision speed and quality, traceable grounds); the four build steps of work selection, data selection, semantic structuring, and the verification cycle (success splits on systematizing verification — 'replace human limits with structure'); the three-track staffing of ontology engineer, IT, and domain experts with tool-drafted ontologies verified by experts; governance (terminology, KPIs, ownership, digitizing tacit knowledge) and the living ontology that stores executions and their evaluations; and a starting guide where the company that pays off its 'data debt' first pulls ahead

relations.evidenceRef: Delegates the definitions and principles of ontology and semantic layer to the concepts part and builds cases, ROI, and the build process on top
